newsitem.title: UK: Options - Coffee, cocoa vols steady amid slow trade.
newsitem.headline: Options - Coffee, cocoa vols steady amid slow trade.

text.p: LIFFE coffee and cocoa options volatilities were mostly steady from last week in sluggish activity ahead of a three-day UK holiday weekend.
UK markets are closed on Monday for a bank holiday.
At-the-money July coffee options volatility was seen between 38 percent and 39.5 percent and September between 40 and 42 percent. Both were steady to slightly softer from late last week's levels.
September and November were seen close to 40 percent and January slightly higher near 42 percent to make the curve relatively flat.
Traders noted very little coffee options activity this week. They said volume was 100-lots, mostly scattered between some at-the-money July options with no decipherable pattern seen.

This morning, traders said there was interest in buying November puts, but July grabbed the most interest with 40 July $1,600 and 10 July $1,650 puts changing hands. Total volume for the morning session was near 70 contracts.
In cocoa, activity was even more quiet this week with no options volume on Monday and Tuesday so far despite a sharp price drop on Tuesday.
July cocoa tumbled to the lowest since April 10 on Tuesday on fund and speculative sales.
At-the-money July cocoa options volatility was pegged near 30 percent. September, December and March were each seen near 28 percent.

One trader speculated that part of the reason for sluggish options activity despite price swings in the underlying futures showed that most people were probably on the right side of the market but still did not make a windfall.

He said that "people usually don't use options unless they have lost a lot of money and rush to hedge or protect themselves or the reverse, when you have 'punters' that have made a lot of money" and buy options for as a speculative gamble.
The upcoming three-day holiday weekend in the UK probably also dampened options activity because of time decay.

Though some floor sources said cocoa volatilities could rise on Thursday afternoon if July slips through its recent April 9 low of 980 stg per tonne, volatilities were likely to drop hard from peak levels as the holiday weekend approaches.
The time decay for the third day of a holiday weekend normally starts to get priced in by Friday morning if the underlying futures are not extremely volatile.
At Thursday's midsession break, LIFFE July cocoa futures were down 13 stg at 984 stg per tonne and coffee up $42 at $1,660.
